chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from 'Ali ibn Muhammad and 'Abd Allah ibn Ibrahim al-Ahmar, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Washsha', who said:

I entered upon al-Rida عليه السلام, and before him was a ewer from which he wanted to prepare himself for salat (prayer). So I came near to pour water for him, but he refused that and said: “Stop, O Hasan.”

So I said: Why do you forbid me from pouring it onto your hand? Do you dislike that I should be rewarded? He said: “You would be rewarded, and I would bear a burden.” So I said to him: How is that? He said: “Have you not heard Allah say:
“So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous work and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord.”
And here I am, when I perform wudu (ablution) for salat (prayer)—and it is an act of worship—I dislike that anyone should share with me in it.”

key_terms.أُوزَرُ: I would bear a burden or sin
key_terms.إِبْرِيقٌ: a ewer or water vessel used for pouring
key_terms.الْعِبَادَةُ: worship or devotional service to Allah
key_terms.بِعِبَادَةِ رَبِّهِ: in the worship of his Lord, meaning devotional acts done solely for Allah
key_terms.عَمَلًا صَالِحًا: a righteous deed performed properly for Allah
key_terms.لِلصَّلَاةِ: for salat (prayer), indicating the ritual purpose of the preparation

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam al-Rida عليه السلام refuse to let someone pour water for his wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith shows Imam al-Rida عليه السلام emphasizing sincerity and personal devotion in acts of worship such as wudu (ablution) for salat (prayer). He cites the Quranic principle of not associating anyone in the worship of Allah, applying it to his dislike of having another person participate in his preparatory act of worship.
